steps.do: Before you start: start CALIBER with CALIBER_FEATURE_INTEGRATIONS=true, the lab's MCP server script in CALIBER_MCP_STDIO_PYTHON_SCRIPT_ALLOWLIST, and CALIBER_OPERATOR_USERS / CALIBER_APPROVER_USERS naming lab05-operator / lab05-approver. Create the three accounts, then a workspace mcp-ops (top bar +) and add them as Editor, Reviewer and Viewer under Project access.
steps.see: mcp-ops is selected; the three people are members with those roles.

steps.do: Click Add Server. The server is the lab's own repo_tracker_mcp.py, started by CALIBER over stdio (a loopback HTTP endpoint would be refused by the egress policy).
steps.see: A row repo-tracker reading Runtime ready · local containment.

steps.do: Open the Playground tab, pick repo-tracker under Server, click Test Connection. Nothing is callable yet: discovery is inventory, not authorization.
steps.see: Connection Successful, 6 tools discovered, every tool with an amber Unclassified badge; the selected tool's button reads Classify Tool Before Invoking and is disabled.

steps.where: Integrations › MCP Servers › Playground › Tool Policy
steps.do: For each tool set Allow tool, Requires approval, Side effect level and Rate limit / minute from tool-classification.jsonl and click Save Policy. On issue_write set write first and leave approval off: the save is refused (set requires_approval=true for side_effect_level 'write'). Tick Requires approval and save. create_release stays unallowed.
steps.see: Policy saved. No tool is Unclassified now; create_release wears Blocked, issue_write Approval.

steps.do: Select search_repositories, type language:python topic:mcp into query and click Invoke Tool. Then invoke it again with stars:>>not-a-number.
steps.see: Success with acme/mcp-gateway and acme/mcp-servers-internal and a duration; a row under History (browser memory only). The second call is Failed with the server's own message.

steps.do: Select create_release. Its button is disabled, so the refusal payload comes from the API (POST /mcp-servers/{id}/invoke-tool: success:false, is blocked by policy, duration_ms:0). Then select issue_write, fill repo and title and invoke it: it runs, although it requires approval, because the admin Playground is a break-glass surface.
steps.see: Tool Blocked by Policy (disabled) and This tool is blocked by its saved policy.; then Success for the write.

steps.do: Select search_repositories. Use Add case for six cases (S01 to S06) from calibration-cases.jsonl: name, Test case input JSON, Assertion type output_contains, Assertion value. Save cases, then Run calibration. Change case 1's value to "total_count": 9 and run again, then put it back.
steps.see: Pass rate 100% — 6/6 passed; with the wrong value Pass rate 83% — 5/6 passed and case 1 shows fail.

steps.do: Copy the server id from the row. Fill __SERVER_ID__, __TOOL__=issue_write, __LEVEL__=write, __APPROVAL__=true in a copy of file-issue.workflow.yaml. Import, name it mcp-file-issue, Choose file, Validate dependencies, Import as new. In Run Monitor paste {"repo": "acme/release-notes-bot", "title": "..."} and Run. Approve yourself (refused), approve as lab05-approver in a second session, then Resume.
steps.see: Awaiting approval at node call_tool; the account that triggered this run cannot approve it; a second person must decide; after the second person approves and you Resume, completed.

steps.do: In the editor press Publish (v1 becomes read-only), then Restore as draft for v2 · draft. Close the Run Monitor with its ✕, click call_tool in the Outline, then an empty spot on the canvas to open the workflow settings, and untick Approval under Tool bindings for issue_write. Save, open Run Monitor, paste {"repo": "acme/release-notes-bot", "title": "This must never be filed"} and Run.
steps.see: The run is refused: tool policy requires approval but the workflow binding does not. The server's ledger still shows two issue_write calls.

steps.do: Click Add Server with command /bin/sh and arguments -c echo pwned, register it, and click Test on its row. Then read Operate › Audit Log (filter update_mcp_tool_policy, then calibrate_mcp_tool) and Operate › Observability.
steps.see: Runtime blocked and stdio command '/bin/sh' is not in CALIBER_MCP_STDIO_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST; the audit rows; mcp.repo-tracker.search_repositories and mcp.repo-tracker.issue_write traces and none for create_release.
